basis: Big Lots confirmed the crossing on May 27, 2022. Its consolidated GAAP net sales for fiscal Q1 ended April 30, 2022 were $1,374,714,000, below the $1,544,274,400 cutoff calculated from the prior-year quarter’s $1,625,552,000. The March 3 outlook implied a decline large enough to cross the threshold, but supplied no explicit numeric upper bound for consolidated sales. The full January 11 ICR and March 9 BofA management remarks remain unverified, so the earliest qualifying date remains open.

coverage.detail: December 3, 2021, preceding earnings cycle. The outlook covered Q4 FY2021 comparable sales and EPS. The FY2022 sales expectation covered the full year.

December 3 call. Management identified Q1 FY2022 as the toughest stimulus comparison. The five-point estimate described the prior stimulus benefit to full-year comparable sales. It supplied no Q1 consolidated revenue endpoint.

January 10 update. The $8 billion to $10 billion sales target was long-term. The current trading update covered Q4 FY2021. Big Lots scheduled the January 11 ICR fireside chat for 10:30 a.m. ET and advertised an issuer-site replay through January 21.

The January investor deck is accessible as SEC Exhibit 99.2. Its long-term financial goals supply no explicit Q1 FY2022 consolidated sales ceiling. The exhibit contains slides, leaving the spoken discussion unresolved.
ICR’s January 3 host notice confirms presentations moved to its virtual platform. Its schedule and registration links yielded no Big Lots recording or transcript.
ICR’s historical schedule link identified this PDF as its destination. The direct PDF was inaccessible during verification.

The issuer’s advertised webcast and replay location returned HTTP 404. Date-targeted Wayback requests for [January 11](https://web.archive.org/web/20220111/https://www.biglots.com/corporate/investors/) and [March 9](https://web.archive.org/web/20220309/https://www.biglots.com/corporate/investors/) were inaccessible through the web tool. Whether either snapshot preserved a player remains unknown.

March 3 Q4 FY2021 release. Big Lots translated its Q1 FY2022 comparable-sales forecast of approximately 10% growth over 2019 into a low-double-digit comparable-sales decline versus 2021. The explicit $1.10–$1.20 range applied to diluted EPS.

March 3, slide 21. Alongside the Q1 comparable-sales outlook, Big Lots projected a 130-basis-point sales benefit from net new and relocated stores. Illustratively, a 10% comp decline plus 1.3 percentage points implies about an 8.7% consolidated decline. That calculation is a secondary observation. Management gave no numeric consolidated endpoint.
March 3 earnings call. The CFO described the Q1 store contribution as roughly 130 basis points and repeated the comparable-sales outlook.

The prior review located the March 4 conference announcement in the issuer’s wire listing. Live search independently surfaced the May 13 notice scheduling Q1 results for May 27. Direct retrieval of the listing returned a cache miss. The interval search found no written Q1 consolidated sales preannouncement.

March 9 BofA Consumer & Retail Technology Conference. A contemporaneous [participant event page](https://corporate.walmart.com/news/events/bank-of-america-securities-2022-consumer-retail-technology-conference) identified the host’s VeraCast directory. The directory was inaccessible. No Big Lots-specific host replay or deck was recovered.

A transcript listing independently identifies Big Lots’ March 9 session at 10:30 a.m. Its public preview ends during BofA moderator Jason Haas’s introduction. Management’s remarks are subscriber-only, so the preview cannot establish what guidance management gave.

The [proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/768835/000110465922045520/tm222356-1_def14a.htm) scheduled the May 24 annual meeting at headquarters. Item 5.07 reports the votes. Item 2.02 separately dates the earnings release to May 27. The filing supplies no transcript of annual-meeting remarks.

May 27 actuals. The consolidated net-sales row gives 1,374,714 and 1,625,552 in thousands of dollars for the quarters ended April 30, 2022 and May 1, 2021. Big Lots reported a 15.4% total sales decline, a 17.0% comparable-sales decline and approximately 1.6 percentage points of growth from net new stores and relocations.

publication_date_evidence: The issuer’s [wire release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/big-lots-reports-q1-results-301556383.html) is timestamped May 27, 2022 at 6:00 a.m. ET, matching the dateline in SEC Exhibit 99.1 and the release date stated in the covering 8-K. This verifies when actuals became public. The missing conference remarks prevent assigning that date as the earliest disclosure.
